question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6},\, & 0\le x\le 6, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{6}x\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{x}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{12}|}_{0}^{6} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{6}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{18}|}_{0}^{6} \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =12-{(3)}^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
